CVE-2026-135844.description: The fix for CVE-2026-61801 added file type and size checks when parsing user and group files in github.com/moby/sys/user, but did not apply them consistently across all parsing and lookup functions. ParsePasswdFile, ParsePasswdFileFilter, GetAdditionalGroupsPath, ParseSubIDFile, ParseSubIDFileFilter, ParseIDMapFile, ParseIDMapFileFilter, LookupUser, LookupUid, LookupGroup and LookupGid could still read large or unbounded files. An attacker who controls the contents of a user or group file processed by an affected application, such as /etc/passwd or /etc/group from a container image, can cause excessive memory or CPU consumption, resulting in a denial of service. Exploitation depends on how the consuming application uses the affected functions. Fixed in v0.5.1 by enforcing the 10 MiB read limit in all affected functions. Docker Engine 29.10.1 includes the fix.

CVE-2026-61801.description: The `github.com/moby/sys/user` package provides Go utilities for parsing and looking up entries in Unix-style user and group database files. Versions before 0.4.1 do not sufficiently limit entries when parsing `/etc/passwd`- or `/etc/group`-style files, allowing an attacker who can supply a specially crafted file to cause excessive memory consumption and potentially terminate the affected process due to an out-of-memory condition. This issue is patched in version 0.4.1. As a workaround, avoid parsing attacker-controlled user or group database files, or validate and limit untrusted input before parsing it.
